headline: Brijgopal Bang files SEBI Takeover Regulation 31(4) disclosure for Thomas Scott (India) Limited
sum: SEBI takeover disclosure filing by Brijgopal Bang under Regulation 31(4) for Thomas Scott (India) Limited, lodged with NSE on 6 May 2026.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure marks a mandatory public filing gate post-acquisition of substantial shares or control; the filing itself does not confirm acquisition completion but triggers disclosure obligations and potential open offer compliance review under Regulations 3–5.
detail: Brijgopal Bang has submitted to NSE a disclosure filing under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4). This regulation requires disclosure of acquisitions that cross the 25% threshold or trigger a change of control. The filing is archived in the NSE corporate filings portal. Specific acquisition value, shareholding percentage acquired, and transaction structure are not disclosed in the available reference.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of substantial acquisitions post-completion or material change; triggers public disclosure to stock exchange.
Defines 'Substantial Acquisition' (25% or more in listed entity); triggers open offer obligation if acquisition leads to change of control.
Prescribes conditions and process for voluntary open offers above 25% threshold.
Defines mandatory open offer trigger (acquisition of 25% or more, or change of control).
Director identification number (DIN) and beneficial ownership disclosure; cross-referenced in takeover filings.
Disclosure of Material Events and Information to exchanges; takeover filings often trigger listing regulation compliance.
Exemptions and conditions for acquisitions (e.g., preferential allotments, inter-se transfers); may apply to this acquisition.

conditions: Acquisition (if any) crosses 25% shareholding threshold or triggers change of control
Mandatory disclosure filing with stock exchange within 2 business days post-acquisition completion (Reg 31(4))
Potential open offer obligation if regulation 10 trigger satisfied
approvals: Possible CCI review if acquisition value exceeds threshold (₹2,250 cr combined turnover for Indian entities)
structure.novel: No novel structural element identified from available disclosure reference.

triggers.note: Mandatory disclosure filing post-acquisition or material change; triggers public filing obligation.
If acquisition crosses 25% or leads to change of control, open offer obligations may be triggered.
If combined turnover exceeds ₹2,250 cr, combination notification to CCI required within 30 days.
